channel.title: DevPulse · Inference
channel.description: Daily inference stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: LoopCD improves looped-transformer scores while cutting recurrent compute
item.description: Training-free LoopCD raises Ouro-2.6B-Thinking AIME 2024 pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33% and cuts forward FLOPs by 22.5–48.2% when fewer loops suffice. It turns intermediate recurrent predictions into a decoding signal that can improve quality and reduce inference compute.

item.title: AgSpec adapts retrieval-based speculative decoding to coding agents
item.description: AgSpec retrieves drafts from session, workspace and global corpora, then adapts draft length using verification feedback; it reports up to 4.37× throughput at batch size 1 and 4.76× at batch size 16. The results show how agent-specific context and acceptance behavior can improve inference speed.

item.title: Helion’s vLLM linear backend improves throughput with per-shape kernel autotuning
item.description: The backend uses one Helion GEMM implementation with per-shape autotuning and hybrid dispatch across algorithm variants; on Hopper GPUs, it outperformed the evaluated CUTLASS and DeepGEMM backends, with over 10% throughput gains on some workloads. This shows how a higher-level kernel DSL can improve inference performance while reducing implementation complexity.

item.title: Janus serves GGUF models locally through Vulkan and an OpenAI-compatible API
item.description: Janus is a single Go binary that runs GGUF models through Vulkan or a CPU fallback, exposes chat-completions endpoints and supports model hot-swapping. It offers a low-dependency local-serving option, though the listing provides no performance results.

item.title: OpenDLSS reimplements Nvidia’s neural rendering network in Vulkan and WebGPU
item.description: The project reports byte-for-byte matching at all 75 block boundaries for a 71-block network, with a Vulkan FP8 implementation and an independent WebGPU port. Reproducing model execution across GPU and browser runtimes is a substantial engineering reference.

item.title: Phonon-2 reaches 5.21% average English word error in a 164 MB model
item.description: Phonon-2 uses roughly 2.1-bit learned weight levels and reports 5.21% average word error across seven English test sets, with high throughput on CPUs and an H100. Its results show the accuracy and serving-speed trade-offs possible with a compact ASR model.

item.title: TensorRT RTX samples pair ONNX Runtime with native C++ inference
item.description: The samples separate Python-based model export to ONNX from C++ deployment, with reported GPU results including 39× real-time Nemotron ASR and 38.3 FPS for SAM 2.1. Engineers building local inference apps can use the examples to evaluate deployment patterns and acceleration.

item.title: WUSH-KV uses data-adaptive transforms for low-bit KV-cache quantization
item.description: Integrated into SGLang, the method reports that at 2-bit it matches or outperforms the OSCAR transform across evaluated models and downstream tasks. Lower KV-cache cost can extend the context or batch sizes available to inference services.

item.title: FlexKV caching cuts HSTU recommender latency by up to 5.93×
item.description: An HSTU inference workflow combines AOTI-compiled models with FlexKV caching; at batch size 8, caching cut latency by up to 5.93× on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. The measured gain and deployment workflow are useful for engineers serving sequence-based recommenders.

item.title: Magnitude targets fast local inference for concurrent agent sessions
item.description: Magnitude says its inference engine tunes and compiles kernels on-device for local agent workloads, and claims speeds up to 2x llama.cpp. Its focus on concurrent sessions and hardware-specific optimization makes the project relevant to local agent serving.

item.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway Auto Router reports up to 30% internal cost savings
item.description: The public-beta router selects a model for each request, and Cloudflare reports up to 30% savings versus using frontier models alone in an internal OpenCode test. Engineers managing model spend can weigh this approach against task-specific routing.

item.title: DeepSeek’s KV-cache optimization is claimed to cut footprint 437× in some long-context cases
item.description: The excerpt claims a DeepSeek KV-cache optimization reduces footprint by roughly 437× for some long-session workloads compared with DeepSeek-V1. The claim is highly relevant to inference costs, but the excerpt gives no method or evidence.

item.title: Claude services recovered after an hour of elevated errors and sign-in failures
item.description: Claude.ai, Claude Code, Cowork and the API experienced errors from 14:00 to 14:59 UTC, with sign-in failures and some unsaved messages reported. The incident shows the breadth of user-facing impact when a shared AI service degrades, though no cause is given.

item.title: Cloudflare User Insights connects AI model usage to task context
item.description: User Insights now relates users, agents, tasks, models, costs, and conversation patterns, and flags when a model may be more capable than a task requires. This can help teams investigate model spend beyond raw request and token counts.

item.title: Startup model strategies balance frontier APIs with open models
item.description: The piece argues that relying on frontier APIs can strain latency, infrastructure overhead and margins as products scale, especially with high-frequency tasks and multi-agent workflows. Engineers can use those pressures to assess when a mixed model-serving strategy may be appropriate.

item.title: Jevstiller uses a disagreement bound to route confident labels to a local model
item.description: Jevstiller trains a CPU-local model to match a vendor’s labels on a target share of requests, reporting about 15 ms latency versus 300 ms remotely. Its agreement contract and threshold selection matter for low-latency classification in agent loops.

item.title: Seven ESP32 boards run a distributed 1.58-bit, 0.5B language model
item.description: The project slices a 0.5B model across seven ESP32-S3 boards, with a master handling tokenization and embeddings and other nodes running transformer layers over SPI. It offers a concrete look at the trade-offs in highly constrained distributed inference.

item.title: Prompt-lookup drafting in llama.cpp gets up to 42× faster with less memory
item.description: The author reports optimizations that make prompt-lookup drafting up to 42× faster while using up to 2.6× less memory; a follow-up contribution raises the reported speedup to 140×. These results make the implementation relevant to engineers tuning speculative decoding in inference engines.

item.title: DSX MaxLPS raises GPU throughput 49.2% within the same power budget
item.description: In an evaluation, DSX MaxLPS ran 192 GPUs instead of 140 within a 264.4 kW budget, raising aggregate throughput 49.2%; P99 time to first token rose 17%. The results show why capacity gains need to be weighed against tail latency.

item.title: An ESP32-S3 pedal runs neural amp models with hand-written kernels
item.description: The pedal runs 23-layer WaveNet amp models at 48 kHz, using block floating point, hand-written Xtensa kernels, two cores, and 64-frame blocks; the same firmware also builds to WebAssembly. It is a concrete example of bringing neural inference to constrained hardware.

item.title: FLEET uses generation history to reduce duplicate sampling and improve coding results
item.description: FLEET adjusts logits using sparse, high-entropy generation trajectories; it reports 3× speedup at baseline accuracy and raises LiveCodeBench Pass@32 from 59.9% to 66.2% at the same budget. The method connects decoding decisions to prior samples rather than treating each draw independently.

item.title: Confidential inference retains up to 98.2% of baseline throughput on B200 GPUs
item.description: On eight B200 GPUs running DeepSeek-R1, confidential compute retained 96.1%–98.2% of baseline output-token throughput with 1.2%–4.3% per-token latency overhead. The implementation details show how memory protection affects inference performance and data movement.

item.title: TensorRT multi-GPU serving cuts Cosmos generation latency from 156.6 to 34.2 seconds
item.description: A single TensorRT model instance distributed across eight GPUs reduced Cosmos 3 Nano generation latency from 156.6 to 34.2 seconds. The integration shows how multi-device execution can simplify serving while retaining a single gRPC endpoint.

item.title: PISA uses hierarchical Top-K selection for O(N log N) sparse attention
item.description: PISA narrows attention candidates through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy, with Triton kernels that fuse routing and scoring without materializing the query-key matrix. Its stated O(N log N) complexity targets a major bottleneck in long-context attention.

item.title: Google Cloud outlines networking choices for AI inference across GPUs and TPUs
item.description: The guide considers accelerator availability and networking configuration for private LLM inference, including GPU and TPU options. Teams planning flexible deployments can use the trade-offs to account for network setup alongside accelerator choice.

item.title: Prompting GLM-5.3-Flash enables one-pass decisions competitive with Jev
item.description: The approach makes the first output token the decision, using one forward pass; its accuracy and speed match Jev and beat Laya, while costing several times more per decision than Jev. It gives engineers a measured trade-off for low-latency decisions and supports vision inputs.

item.title: LLM token log probabilities enable compact classification responses
item.description: A prompt can constrain a classification answer to one token, then use API log probabilities to compare candidate labels. This can reduce generated output and offers a useful inference pattern for classification workloads.

item.title: GeoPair compresses transformers by factorizing compatible cross-layer weights
item.description: GeoPair pairs structurally compatible projections and factorizes them with shared dictionaries, preserving layer-specific calibration geometry without training. Its reported gains over independent and heuristic decompositions make it relevant to engineers evaluating model compression.

item.title: Hugging Face hires oMLX maintainer to support local AI on Apple Silicon
item.description: Jun Kim will continue maintaining oMLX, an Apache 2.0 project built around MLX for local AI on Apple Silicon, with the post citing more stability and funded development. Sustained maintenance matters for engineers choosing local inference tools.

item.title: Ollaya runs local decision models in a single forward pass
item.description: Ollaya runs decision models locally without token-by-token generation; its example reports about 10 ms end to end for five questions on an RTX 4090. Fast local decisions could be useful in agent workflows where each action needs a lightweight risk check.

item.title: A daily model-value chart maps LLM capability against token cost
item.description: The tool plots model intelligence against blended input and output token prices, identifies the value frontier and shows daily changes in models and pricing. Engineers choosing models for a budget can compare cost and capability in one place.

item.title: Parakeet Redux fits in 178 MB and runs at 113× real time on CPU
item.description: Parakeet Redux uses 1.58-bit weights and runs at 113× real time on eight x86 CPU cores; its 178 MB size comes with English WER within 0.3 points of the original and stronger results on some listed benchmarks. The results make it a concrete example of aggressive quantization for fast, compact speech recognition.

item.title: vLLM adds hardware-agnostic layers with 3.4% throughput cost on H100
item.description: New vLLM layers aim to preserve portability as the project optimizes around torch.compile; on H100, throughput is within 3.4% of the native implementation across three models. This gives teams a measured view of the trade-off between peak performance and accelerator portability.

item.title: Google tests whether AI hardware can survive in space
item.description: Project Suncatcher is testing a prototype satellite to see whether AI chips withstand radiation, vibration and the cooling challenges of a vacuum. The engineering constraints matter to anyone evaluating unconventional ways to scale compute.

item.title: GPT-6 prompt caching adds diagnostics and explicit breakpoints
item.description: GPT-6 prompt caching adds diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, higher cache hit rates, and controls intended to reduce latency and cost. These mechanisms matter to teams tuning inference performance and serving economics.

item.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna cut listed prices versus their GPT-5.6 counterparts
item.description: The excerpt lists GPT-6 Luna at half the input and output prices of GPT-5.6 Luna, with a similar reduction for Sol, and compares several models’ token rates. Those prices can change model selection and the economics of production workloads.
